title: Normalize option premium by volatility, like a Sharpe ratio
summary: When you sell covered calls or cash-secured puts, the premium alone does not tell you if you are paid enough. The speaker divides the premium by the volatility of the underlying, the same way a Sharpe ratio divides returns by standard deviation. That gives context and lets you compare trades apples to apples.

params.label: IV premium over RV
params.help: Average points that implied vol trades above realized vol.

steps.caption: One year of a stock and its volatility. Premium only makes sense next to this risk.
The price path. Bigger swings mean more risk for the option seller.
Realized volatility is the risk you take: the standard deviation of the stock's returns.
Implied volatility sets the premium you collect.
Premium divided by volatility works like a Sharpe ratio: yield per unit of risk.

takeaways: Premium needs context: compare it with the risk of the underlying.
Dividing yield by volatility is like a Sharpe ratio for option selling.
A normalized number lets you compare different stocks on one scale.
caveats: The speaker's screener, Discord and website are promotional and not verified here.
The clip gives no exact formula or numbers for the metric.
